transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-07-21
Start: 14:00 UTC
Duration: ~47 minutes
Attendees: Maya Patel (Redwood AE), Jon Ramos (Redwood SE), Sara Kim (CTO, Equinox), Liam O'Connor (Platform Eng), Priya Desai (Security), Evan Holt (Data Scientist)

Auto-summary (brief):
- Kickoff to scope POC for inference/eval focused on security/compliance gates and throughput KPIs.
- Key success criteria: p95 latency target, throughput targets, quality thresholds on evaluation prompts, and SOC2/ISO controls, SSO + RBAC + audit logs requirements.
- Action items: Redwood to share compliance artifacts, draft benchmark runbook; Equinox to share workload traces and stakeholders.

Topics: success criteria, workload sizing, benchmark configuration, SOC 2/ISO and SSO/SAML, RBAC, audit logs, timeline

Transcript body:
[00:00] Maya (Redwood): All right, everyone, thanks for joining. Quick roll call—I'm Maya, AE on this. Jon from infra/SE is with me.
[00:08] Jon (Redwood): hi all, jon here. we'll try to keep this pragmatic, sorry for the slightly delayed start.
[00:13] Sara (Equinox): No worries, thanks. Sara here. We've got a lot of moving parts so this kickoff helps.
[00:18] Liam (Equinox): Liam, platform eng. I'll be the point on logs and infra.
[00:23] Priya (Equinox): Priya, security. I'll escalate any compliance gaps.
[00:26] Evan (Equinox): Evan, data science — I'll own the eval set and quality gating.

[00:30] Maya: Cool. Goal for today: align on what success looks like for the POC, get a ballpark of workload sizing so we can propose a benchmark config, and cover the security/compliance gates you need during the pilot — SOC 2/ISO, SSO, RBAC, audit logs, KMS.
[00:43] Sara: That sounds right. We're evaluating whether to go hosted or dedicated for the pilot but security is non-negotiable. We'll need SOC2 evidence and SSO flow for Okta. Also, audit log retention requirements — we'll outline them.
[00:55] Jon: Understood. Quick question on success metrics — do you have an existing SLA or target numbers?
[01:02] Evan: For our first pass we want p95 response latency under ~120 ms on our normal prompt distribution, throughput of about 150 req/s sustained, with bursts up to 400 rps for short windows. Quality: our eval harness needs >0.86 F1 on the regression prompts we sent last week.
[01:19] Jon: Good, that's actionable. Roughly, to hit p95 120 ms for that mix we'll propose instance sizing and batching config; we'll also show a fallback to a cheaper quantized model if latency slips.
[01:30] Priya: On security — SOC 2 Type II is required for any hosted vendor; ISO27001 would be ideal but we can accept ISO summary for pilot. We need SSO via SAML (Okta), RBAC scoped to environment and model access, and audit logs with at least 90-day retention for the pilot. Also, encryption: BYOK preferred, KMS integration required.
[01:52] Maya: Thanks, Priya. We'll share SOC 2 Type II attestation and ISO summary — and a SSO/SAML integration guide showing Okta and ADFS flows. For RBAC we can show role templates (admin, dev, observer) and how they map to APIs in the console. For audit logs we have streaming to S3 or to your SIEM — retention configurable.
[02:10] Liam: When you say streaming logs, can you push to our existing CloudWatch / Splunk? We prefer not to pull.
[02:15] Jon: Yes, push is supported. We can stream audit events and per-request traces to your destination via a secure connector; we'll include a sample CloudWatch setup in the runbook.
[02:25] Sara: Great. On data residency — half our prompts are EU-regulated. For the pilot we need processing in eu-west region and no replica in other regions. Is that doable on hosted?
[02:36] Maya: We can pin region for the pilot; Redwood hosted has region pinning. For Private/Dedicated we'd obviously keep it VPC / on-prem as you prefer.
[02:42] Evan: Workload sizing — here's a summary from our side: average daily queries ~200k, median prompt length 120 tokens, average generation 80 tokens, peak QPS 420 for 2–3 minute bursts, payloads include some structured fields. We'll drop a 7-day anonymized trace to S3 link after the call.
[03:05] Jon: Perfect — that trace will let us pick realistic sequence length distribution. For benchmarking we usually run a 1-hour soak at target throughput and then 10x burst tests to validate autoscaling. We'll also run isolated per-model latency tests (cold vs warm KV cache).
[03:22] Sara: Can you define 'cold vs warm' in the runbook? Our engineers need to know warm cache assumptions.
[03:28] Jon: Sure. Warm means KV cache primed for previously-seen conversation contexts; cold means fresh token generation with no cache. We'll log cache hit ratios. Sorry, sometimes our transcript tools write KV cash — but it's cache.
[03:42] Priya: A few compliance questions: 1) Are logs tamper-evident? 2) Do you support field-level redaction? 3) Who has access to raw request data?
[03:50] Maya: Short answers: 1) Yes, logs are append-only and checksummed for tamper-evidence. 2) We support configurable redaction rules and auto-PII masking at ingestion. 3) For hosted pilot, Redwood ops won't look at raw requests unless there's an incident and we have an access request process; otherwise data is isolated to your account. We'll include our access audit workflow.
[04:10] Priya: Ok, we also need proof of background checks and SOC 2 scope — does your SOC 2 cover your infra team?
[04:16] Maya: SOC 2 Type II includes developer and operations control coverage; we'll attach the scope page.
[04:22] Liam: About SSO: we use Okta with SAML 2.0 and SCIM for provisioning. We need just-in-time provisioning and group sync for roles. Does Redwood support SCIM?
[04:32] Jon: SCIM provisioning is supported for team sync; JIT login via SAML also works. We'll send the SAML metadata and a SCIM setup guide.
[04:38] Evan: For quality gating — we need to run an eval suite: 2,000 prompts that cover domain-specific edge cases. During the POC we want an automated regression alert if metrics drop >2% vs baseline. Can we wire that into Redwood Optimize?
[04:52] Maya: Yes, Redwood Optimize can run evals and set alert thresholds. We'll configure a regression alert tied to the prompt set you provide.
[04:58] Sara: Timeline — we want a 4-week pilot: week 1 data handoff + infra config, week 2 benchmark runs and tuning, week 3 integration and SSO onboarding, week 4 acceptance and decision. Is that feasible?
[05:10] Jon: That is feasible; we'll need the 7-day traces and stakeholder signoff quickly to meet week1 goals.
[05:15] Maya: Real quick on success criteria recap — we'll write this down and put it in the runbook: 1) p95 latency <= 120 ms on your eval mix, 2) sustained throughput 150 req/s with 400 rps bursts without >5% error rate, 3) quality threshold (Evan's eval) >= 0.86 F1, 4) SOC2 Type II evidence provided, SSO + RBAC configured, 90-day audit logs retained and streamed to customer's destination.
[05:36] Sara: That matches internal expectations. A question on cost — we need a pilot cost estimate (hosted) and an estimate for Dedicated. Can you give a ballpark now?
[05:45] Maya: Ballpark: hosted pilot for your workload estimate ~ $12k-$18k for the month depending on model variant and request mix; dedicated reserved capacity jumps to a larger upfront commit but lowers unit cost by ~30%. We'll follow up with a precise pricing sheet once we size hardware per your traces.
[06:02] Liam: For dedicated we'd want SLA and VLAN isolation — also support for KMS BYOK.
[06:08] Jon: Dedicated supports customer-managed KMS and VPC peering; we'll outline network diagrams in the runbook.
[06:14] Priya: A technical detail on audit logs: we need immutable request/response hashes and user attribution (who triggered the call). Is user attribution included in the log schema?
[06:23] Jon: Yes, log schema includes request_id, user_id, role, model_id, latency, cost estimate, and a response-hash for integrity verification. We'll send the schema sample.
[06:33] Evan: For benchmarking, can you run quantized vs FP16 comparisons? We want to see quality delta for 4-bit/8-bit quantization since cost matters.
[06:42] Jon: Absolutely. We'll include a quantization matrix and measure model quality delta vs throughput and cost-per-token. We'll also test an alternate variant that has a lower-context-length profile.
[06:50] Sara: Are there any blockers you foresee for the timeline?
[06:54] Jon: Biggest potential blockers: delay in sample trace delivery, delays on Okta SAML metadata exchange, or any network firewall rules preventing our temporary test egress.
[07:03] Maya: We'll prepare an onboarding checklist and share today: SOC2 docs, SAML metadata template, preliminary runbook, and a proposed benchmark slot next Wednesday.
[07:12] Liam: We'll try to provide traces by Friday. Also, for the SAML exchange we need a short security questionnaire answered; can you fill that?
[07:20] Maya: Yes, we'll fill and return the questionnaire — Jon will own the technical Qs.
[07:24] Priya: One more: incident response SLA during pilot — can you commit to 2-hour critical incident response?
[07:30] Maya: For pilot we can commit to a vendor on-call with 2-hour response; enterprise SLA can be tighter under contract. We'll include point-of-contact details.
[07:40] Sara: ok great. Let's call out acceptance criteria again and ensure the runbook maps to them.
[07:45] Maya: Will do. To recap next steps: Maya to send SOC2/ISO summary + SAML/SCIM guides; Jon to prepare benchmark runbook and log schema; Equinox to provide traces, identify stakeholders, and fill the security questionnaire. We'll propose benchmark dates and a detailed cost sheet once traces land.
[08:02] Evan: Quick clarifying Q — how is KV cache warmed in a multi-tenant hosted setup? We have many small convos, so warm cache may be low.
[08:12] Jon: We can pre-populate KV cache for the benchmark with synthetic traffic that mirrors your conversation prefixes; we'll also show hit-rate targets. For multi-tenant isolation, we have per-tenant cache buckets.
[08:25] Maya: Any other questions?
[08:28] Priya: Not for now — thanks. We'll review the artifacts once you share them.
[08:32] Sara: Thanks everyone, that was helpful.
[08:35] Maya: Great, thanks all — we'll follow up with the docs and schedule.

(Conversation continues — minor technical clarifications and scheduling notes, ends at ~47:00)
